experiment.name: phase2_tier3_covert
_comment: Tier 3: the receiver reads nothing at all. It runs its own fixed
instruction stream and times it with rdtsc, so unlike tier 2 there is no
file to revoke and no interface a container can decline to mount. That
makes it the hardest of the three to defend against and the most
Same preconditions as tier 2, for the same reason: Config-B, and ten
victim threads so that something is actually limiting. A hand check
before writing this spec found the receiver's own workload stretched from
1,401,990 TSC under the all-zero operand to 1,639,579 under all-ones, a
17% dilation, against an idle baseline of 1,353,437.
The rate range starts where tier 2 succeeded rather than where it failed.
Tier 3's noise is much worse than tier 2's -- the hand check put the
workload's coefficient of variation above 100% under load against 5% idle
-- so there is no reason to expect it to reach further, and 1 bit/s is
included in case it does not reach as far.
500 us per sample is a compromise: shorter samples resolve a chip better
but each one carries proportionally more rdtsc and lfence overhead, and
the fences are not optional (see the note in rx_timing.c).
aa_1000ms is the control, at the same load and rate as a live row.
